steps.text: Rice (45/70 g dry) on with the kidney beans (70/90 g), a sprig of thyme, the spring onion (20/25 g) and a spoonful of coconut (3/5 g) in the water. 20 minutes, covered.
Salmon (80/105 g) rubbed with jerk paste (8/10 g) and left while the rice cooks.
Grill the salmon 10–12 minutes at medium-high, not turned. It's done when it flakes at a light press and is still coral in the middle.
Pineapple (70/90 g) in thick slices onto a dry griddle, high, 2 minutes a side until it caramelises and marks. Chop.
Slaw: red cabbage (80/100 g), the charred pineapple, lime, salt and the oil (4/5 g).
Cauliflower (120/150 g) stirred through the rice for the last 2 minutes, lid on, to steam.

why: Char the pineapple. Raw, it is just sweet against an already sweet-hot fish; caramelised, it picks up a bitter edge and that is the thing stopping the whole plate from cloying.
notes: D0-003: the pineapple-slaw oil is a raw finishing/dressing use → olive_oil.

D0-014 (Sunday cabbage 515 g): this dish's red_cabbage (80/100 g) is the THIRD consumer PLAN §4 flags as missing from the original Sunday op text (the op named only Thursday's burger and Friday's wrap) — see prep-a.json for the corrected 515 g / three-consumer fix.

Seasoning weighing: 'salmon rubbed with jerk paste' and 'a spoonful of coconut in the water' were never gram-tracked. Standard-reference jerk_paste (wet marinade, distinct product from the dry jerk_seasoning used on the chickpeas) added at a realistic rub quantity (8/10 g); coconut_des (already an established Week A ingredient) added at a realistic spoonful, split proportional to the rice dry-weight share (3/5 g). Combined drift +32/+48 kcal — her crosses the 30 kcal note threshold; both additions are named explicitly in PLAN §4's audit ('honey, sugar, soy, mirin, adobo, coconut, suya carry real calories').
